fixes.explanation: Seven, friend? That's a fine number. It's just not the one in the verse. Genesis 16:3 says Abram had lived in Canaan for ten years when Sarai gave her maidservant Hagar to him. Ten years of living in the land, and Sarai still has no child. That's a long stretch of waiting.

Forty is a big number, friend. The Bible uses it in other places, like the rain in Genesis 7:12. But this verse is smaller than that. Genesis 16:3 says Abram had lived in Canaan for ten years when Sarai gave Hagar to him. Ten, not forty.

Hiding in Abram's tent isn't what the text says, friend. Genesis 16:6 says Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her. Then verse 7 finds Hagar by a spring in the desert. She ran, she didn't hide.

Keep going and never return? The angel says the opposite. He tells Hagar, "Return to your mistress and submit to her authority." Hagar had just said she was running away from Sarai. I bet she didn't expect to hear that one.

True. The angel says, "I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count." That's a big promise for a woman who has just been found by a spring in the desert. And it comes from the angel of the LORD himself.

False is right. The angel says Ishmael will be "…a wild donkey of a man…" and that "he will live in hostility toward all his brothers." That's the opposite of living in peace. I think this is a heavy part of the passage, and the text doesn't soften it.

The God of my fathers is a name that shows up in other places, like Exodus 3:15. But it isn't what Hagar says here. She says, "You are the God who sees me…" She says it about the LORD who spoke to her by the spring. Her name for Him comes from what just happened to her.

Eighty-six! Look at you, baker. Genesis 16:16 says, "Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him." I can't even remember what I did last year, and you've got Abram's age on the dot. That's a keeper of a number.

Ninety-nine is a real age in Abram's story, friend, but the story hasn't gotten there yet. Genesis 16:16 says Abram was eighty-six when Hagar bore Ishmael to him. Hold onto that ninety-nine for later.
